candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule was discovered on the central lower eyelid
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
candidates.why: The patient's eyelid mass and histopathological examination results are consistent with squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: Sebaceous carcinoma
support_spans: Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
contradict_spans: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
candidates.why: The clear cell change and periodic acid-Schiff positivity could suggest sebaceous carcinoma, but negative adipophilin and androgen receptor stains contradict this.
candidates.axis_node: Eyelid tumor with clear cell change

candidates.name: Actinic keratosis
support_spans: Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
contradict_spans: Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
candidates.why: The hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts could suggest actinic keratosis, but the presence of malignant squamous cells contradicts this.

candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei
candidates.why: The Ki67 staining results are decisive in confirming the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma.
